title: APPLE: Toward General Active Perception via Reinforcement Learning
claim: A single shared-backbone model closes the loop between observation, action and prediction, and it applies across many tasks.
layout: Closed-loop cycle, top task panel, model box at bottom, clockwise arrows
description: A closed-loop diagram. A gray dotted rounded panel at the top holds four benchmark task renders: Circle-Square (two grayscale squares), Tactile MNIST Volume, Tactile MNIST and Toolbox. Each of the last three shows a gray tactile sensor on a blue plane next to a red 3D object. A blue arrow labeled 'Observation' runs down the right side. It carries stacked grayscale and colored sensor images into the APPLE box at bottom center. Inside the box, three dotted arrows lead right to left through ViT, Vector + Embeddings and Transformer blocks. From there, a 'Prediction' arrow goes left to a bar chart of class probabilities. An 'Action' arrow goes up the left side, past a sensor icon, and back into the task panel. The APPLE logo with an apple sits above the model box. The eye goes first to the top task panel, then follows the loop.
caption: Our method Active Perception Policy Learning (APPLE) aims to infer properties, such as object classes, of its environment based on limited per-step information. To do so, it jointly optimizes an action policy for information gathering and a prediction model for inference. Both the action policy and prediction models use a shared transformer-based backbone to process input sequences. Shown at the top are four benchmark tasks we use to evaluate APPLE.
abstract: Active perception is a fundamental skill that enables us humans to deal with uncertainty in our inherently partially observable environment. For senses such as touch, where the information is sparse and local, active perception becomes crucial. In recent years, active perception has emerged as an important research domain in robotics. However, current methods are often bound to specific tasks or make strong assumptions, which limit their generality. To address this gap, this work introduces APPLE (Active Perception Policy Learning) - a novel framework that leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to address a range of different active perception problems. APPLE jointly trains a transformer-based perception module and decision-making policy with a unified optimization objective, learning how to actively gather information. By design, APPLE is not limited to a specific task and can, in principle, be applied to a wide range of active perception problems. We evaluate two variants of APPLE across different tasks, including tactile exploration problems from the Tactile MNIST benchmark. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of APPLE, achieving high accuracies on both regression and classification tasks. These findings underscore the potential of APPLE as a versatile and general framework for advancing active perception in robotics. Project page: https://timschneider42.github.io/apple
